title: Marriage: the Sisters of Mercy
summary: The only way to win Matchfall. Pass a Sister of Mercy's traditional Catholic examination (five correct answers in a row), get a free wedding ring from one of five Sunfall jewelers, then propose.
fellowship: The Sisters of Mercy are a lay fellowship of traditional Catholic women in Sunfall, not a vowed religious congregation. Every member is free to marry.
timeRule: Time advances only through Start Another Day. No weekdays, calendar dates or clock times are needed to play.

rules.ringArrived: A small velvet box has been delivered. The wedding ring is on your desk.
rules.alreadyHaveRing: You already have a wedding ring on your desk.
dayDone: That’s enough for today. Ask me again tomorrow, and keep studying.
Two is plenty for one day. Come back to me tomorrow.
Let’s stop there for today. I’ll have more questions for you tomorrow.
That will do for today. Pray on it, and we’ll carry on tomorrow.

victory.subtitle: You found your perfect match.
victory.line: You and {name} · St. Brigid’s Chapel · Day {day}

MATCH-007.name: Sophia Moretti
MATCH-007.start: Ask whether she would ever marry you
MATCH-007.player: Sophia… would you ever consider marrying someone like me?
MATCH-007.intro: Marry you? Oh my goodness. Well, darling, if you really expect me to consider marrying you, I suppose we ought to establish whether you know anything about the Catholic faith. Five right in a row. Nonna would insist.
MATCH-007.resume: Back for more? Wonderful. Where were we…
MATCH-007.pause: Of course, darling. I'll keep your place. Go and pray about it!
correct: Oh! You actually knew that one!
Yes! Nonna would be so proud of you.
Look at you, paying attention at Mass!
Correct! I might have to start practicing a new surname.
wrong: Oh no, darling. Back to the start, I'm afraid.
Sweetheart, that's quite embarrassing. Shall we begin again?
Somewhere, Nonna just fainted. From the top!
Not quite! I still like you, though. Again!
MATCH-007.pass: FIVE! Five in a row! I think I just squealed in the parish office. You know your faith… and I think you know my heart a little, too.
MATCH-007.noRing: A girl does need a ring, darling! Go and see a jeweler. I'll wait. Probably.
MATCH-007.accept: A ring?! Yes! Yes, yes, a hundred times yes! I'm calling Nonna. No, I'm calling Father first. No… NONNA!
MATCH-007.dispute: Before we start, darling: you’ll have heard about the bishop and us. Nonna says a man who can pass this can pass anything the chancery sends. So. Five in a row.

MATCH-055.name: Margaret Holloway
MATCH-055.start: Ask whether she would ever consider marriage
MATCH-055.player: Margaret, I'd like to ask you something serious. Would you ever consider marrying me?
MATCH-055.intro: Marriage is a serious undertaking, and I never begin anything without proper preparation. Five correct answers in a row. One mistake and we begin again. Shall we?
MATCH-055.resume: Very well. We continue exactly where we left off.
MATCH-055.pause: Stopping halfway. I'll note it. Don't make a habit of it.
correct: Correct. Next.
Good. Don't get comfortable.
Five minutes with you and I'm almost impressed.
That's right. I've made a note.
wrong: No. We begin again.
Perhaps you ought to spend another evening with your missal.
Incorrect. I did warn you.
I think we had better start again. From the very beginning.
MATCH-055.pass: Five in a row. I… did not expect that. Very well. You follow through, and that matters to me more than I usually admit.
MATCH-055.noRing: A proposal without a ring is a plan without preparation. Come back when it's done properly.
MATCH-055.accept: With a ring, and on your word. Yes. I accept. I'll draw up the guest list tonight, and you will be on time.
MATCH-055.dispute: One thing first. The chancery is reviewing whether we exist. A fellowship that marries and raises its daughters in the faith cannot be reviewed out of existence, which is why I take this seriously. Five in a row.

MATCH-056.name: Teresa Bellamy
MATCH-056.temperament: a teacher who is demanding about religious knowledge
MATCH-056.start: Ask whether she would ever marry you
MATCH-056.player: Teresa, would you ever think about marrying me?
MATCH-056.intro: Oh, I warn you, I'm a teacher. I set examinations for ten-year-olds and I mark them ruthlessly. Five correct in a row, no repeats, no hints. Ready? Pencils down… well, phones up.
MATCH-056.resume: Back to class! Let's pick up where we left off.
MATCH-056.pause: Break time. But the examination will still be here, and so will I.
correct: Correct! Gold star.
Yes! I could give you a whole lesson on that one, but I won't. Not now, anyway.
Very good. My class would be jealous.
Right again. I'm running out of gold stars.
wrong: Ah. No. That one's a classic mistake. Back to the beginning!
I'd have to mark that wrong, I'm afraid. From the top.
Oh dear. I had rather hoped you'd know that.
Detention! I'm joking. Mostly. Start again.
MATCH-056.pass: Five out of five, in a row! Full marks. I'm telling my grandmother. She's been asking whether I'd ever meet a man who knew his Ember days.
MATCH-056.noRing: Without a ring? My grandmother would never let me hear the end of it. She sells them, you know. Bellamy & Daughters, in Old Town.
MATCH-056.accept: Yes! Yes, of course yes. Oh, Granny is going to cry all over the display cases.
MATCH-056.dispute: You know about the review, I expect. The bishop can review the fellowship. He cannot review a marriage. So the examination matters more this season, not less. Gold stars for five in a row.

MATCH-057.name: Evelyn Rosales
MATCH-057.start: Ask whether she would ever consider marrying you
MATCH-057.player: Evelyn, I'll be direct. Would you ever consider marrying me?
MATCH-057.intro: I keep the parish accounts, so I check everything twice. If you're serious, let's see whether you know the faith. Five correct answers, consecutively. I'll be keeping a tally.
MATCH-057.resume: Reopening the ledger. Your tally stands where you left it.
MATCH-057.pause: Ledger closed for now. Nothing's been written off.
correct: Correct. One more tick in the column.
That balances.
Right. I'm still checking your figures.
Correct. I'm cautiously impressed.
wrong: That doesn't add up. Back to zero.
Wrong. I'm resetting the tally.
Oh dear. Let's audit that again from the beginning.
No. I'd have had to send that back with a note.
MATCH-057.pass: Five consecutive. I checked twice. You actually know this. I don't say it often: I trust you.
MATCH-057.noRing: No ring? I can't approve an unfunded proposal. Even a free ring would do.
MATCH-057.accept: A ring, a proper proposal and five correct answers. Everything reconciles. Yes. I'll marry you.
MATCH-057.dispute: I should say, before I ask anything: the chancery is reviewing us, and I keep the minutes of it, and I am not brave in front of people. I can be brave with one person. Five in a row, please.

MATCH-066.name: Priya Nair
MATCH-066.temperament: scholarly, warm and stubborn about principle
MATCH-066.start: Ask whether she would ever marry you
MATCH-066.player: Priya, would you ever consider marrying me?
MATCH-066.intro: You want to marry a librarian? Then you'll be examined. Five questions in a row, from the stacks of my memory. No skimming.
MATCH-066.resume: Welcome back to the reading room. Your place is bookmarked.
MATCH-066.pause: I'll bookmark your page. Come back when you've done some reading.
correct: Correct! Filed under promising.
Yes. You've clearly done the reading.
I see somebody has been paying attention at Mass.
Right again. I may have to give you a reader's card for life.
wrong: Overdue! Back to the beginning.
Not quite. I'm re-shelving you at the start.
Oh, sweetheart. Wrong footnote. Begin again.
Mm, no. Perhaps another evening with the catechism?
MATCH-066.pass: Five in a row. I've cataloged a thousand books and I've never read anything quite as lovely as you getting that last one right.
MATCH-066.noRing: Without a ring? That's a hymn book without a binding. Lovely, but it'll fall apart. Come back with one.
MATCH-066.accept: Yes. With all my heart, yes. I'm going to write this down in the most beautiful hand I have.
MATCH-066.dispute: A note before we begin. The diocese is reviewing the fellowship and the council is reviewing my reading room, and I have filed both under pending. A husband I would file under now. Five in a row.

agnes.name: Agnes Bellamy
agnes.personality: Elderly, sentimental and fond of traditional marriages. Teresa Bellamy's grandmother.
agnes.greeting: Bellamy & Daughters, Agnes speaking. Speak up, dear, the cuckoo clocks are going.

rafael.name: Rafaela Ortega
rafael.greeting: Ortega Repair, Rafaela speaking. What's broken?

clara.name: Clara Whitmore
clara.location: Fifth Avenue, in the gallery district
clara.personality: Elegant, discerning and fascinated by family history. A Bluebird: she wears the blue swallow brooch.
clara.greeting: Whitmore Estate Jewels. Clara Whitmore speaking. If this is about the Bluebird gala, the brooches are spoken for.

joseph.name: Josephine Mercer
joseph.location: A workshop beside the Arizona Canal
joseph.personality: Reserved, meticulous and proud of her craftsmanship.

sofia.name: Sofia Rinaldi
sofia.personality: Cheerful, romantic and enthusiastic about weddings. A Bluebird: she wears the blue swallow brooch.
sofia.greeting: Rinaldi Bridal! Sofia here, still glittery from the Bluebird gala! Are you getting MARRIED?

ask.label: Ask about wedding rings
ask.reply: A wedding ring! Oh, how lovely. Now tell me, dear: is it to be a proper wedding? In church, with a veil and the old Mass?

discount.label: Ask whether she does discounts
discount.reply: Discounts! Young man, a wedding ring is not a can of beans.

church.label: Tell her it will be a proper church wedding
church.reply: Oh, that's what I like to hear. My Walter and I married at St. Brigid's fifty-one years ago. Shall I tell you about it? Everyone hangs up when I start.
church.teresa: My granddaughter Teresa is a Sister of Mercy, you know. Clever girl. Far too clever for most boys.

listen.label: Stay on the line and listen to her story
listen.reply: …and Walter dropped the ring in the font, and Father fished it out with the aspergillum, and we laughed all the way through the Gloria. Oh, I've talked for ages and you listened to every word. There's a plain gold band in my window that's been waiting for someone like you. No, put your wallet away. It's free. Walter would haunt me. It's on its way to you now.

bell.label: Ask what she remembers of the year of the bell
bell.reply: The bell! Oh, dear. I was a young wife. They took it down from St. Brigid’s tower on a truck and rang it at the founders’ fair, and nine ladies from the club sang a round under it, very prettily, and the radio man cut them off. A young priest from the chancery signed for it. Soft hands. I remember his hands, and he is not young now, dear. The bell went up the ridge road on the same truck and never came down. The caretaker who rang it never collected his wages. Walter said never mind. I have minded for forty years.

ask.label: Ask whether she has a plain wedding band
ask.reply: I fix rings, I don't sell many. But there's a plain gold band in my drawer that nobody ever came back for. Tell you what, do me a favor. St. Brigid's sacristy clock has been ready for weeks and nobody's collected it. Call the chapel and let them know?

waiting.label: Ask about the band again
waiting.reply: Deal's still on the table. Call St. Brigid's about their clock first.

done.label: Tell Rafaela the chapel got her message
done.reply: They already called me. The clock's going home, so the ring's going to you. No charge. It was never going to do anyone any good in a drawer. My nephew's dropping it off now.

chapelTopic.label: Tell them Rafaela Ortega has finished the sacristy clock
chapelTopic.reply: Oh, thank goodness. We've been ringing the bell by guesswork for weeks. We'll send someone round. God bless Rafaela.

ask.label: Ask about estate wedding bands
ask.reply: Every ring here has a family history. I only part with them to people who intend to start one. Who is she?

noOne.label: Admit you haven't asked anyone yet
noOne.reply: Then call me back when there's a name, darling. Rings remember.

bride.label: Tell her you hope to marry {name}
bride.reply: {history} There's a plain gold band here from a couple married at St. Brigid's who had sixty years together. It should go back to that church. I won't take a cent for it. My courier is on his way.

history.MATCH-007: Moretti? The Morettis ran the bakery on Brown Avenue for three generations. They baked the bread for every parish picnic.
history.MATCH-055: Holloway? Her great-grandparents gave St. Brigid's its organ.
history.MATCH-056: Bellamy? Agnes Bellamy's granddaughter! Agnes and I have been rivals for forty years. Oh, I would love to beat her to this.
history.MATCH-057: Rosales? Her grandmother sewed the altar linens at St. Brigid's for half a century.
history.MATCH-066: Nair? Her family endowed the parish reading room. She's the one keeping it open, isn't she?

order.label: Ask her to make a plain gold band
order.reply: One ring at a time. Plain gold, polished. Two days. Call back then.

notReady.label: Ask whether the ring is ready
notReady.reply: Not yet. Good work takes the days it takes.

ready.label: Ask whether the ring is ready
ready.reply: It's done. Before it leaves the bench: is it for a marriage, or for a gesture?

gesture.label: Tell her it's to impress someone
gesture.reply: Then buy her flowers. This ring is for a marriage.

marriage.label: Tell her it's for a marriage, for life
marriage.reply: Then it isn't for sale. I don't sell the first ring I make after a quiet month. I give it. Polish it once a year. It's on its way.

ask.label: Tell her you're hoping to get married
ask.reply: AAAH! Tell me everything! How are you going to propose?

app.label: Say you'll propose by message on a dating app
app.reply: On an APP? No, no, no, absolutely not. Try again, tesoro.

drive.label: Say you'll propose with mariachis at a drive-through

knee.label: Say you'll go down on one knee after Mass
knee.reply: On one knee, after Mass?! I'm crying. Okay, this month's Most Romantic Proposal prize is a free wedding band, and it's YOURS. Send me a photo from the wedding! I'm couriering it now.

haveRing.label: Tell them you already have your ring
haveRing.reply: Then what are you doing on the phone with me? Go and ask her!

questions.question: Darling, before you ask my father for my hand, can you tell me the precise date Bishop François Charrière established the Society of Saint Pius X?
A gentleman really ought to know his bishops. Who authorised the SSPX's original foundation in Lausanne, Geneva and Fribourg?
You suggest a romantic visit to Écône. Lovely! Now, which Swiss canton would you actually be taking me to?
When our future children ask about Archbishop Lefebvre's missionary life, which African archdiocese will you tell them he led?
I do hope my future husband remembers the great missionary congregations. Which one elected Lefebvre Superior General in 1962?
I've saved a place for you beside me at our Lefebvre reading evening. On what exact date did he issue his famous declaration?
If you're to impress my family at Sunday lunch, can you name the SSPX Superior General serving in October 2026?
Before I even consider trusting you with our family history timeline, on which date were the four original SSPX bishops consecrated?
We are looking at photographs of the 1988 consecrations. Which retired Brazilian bishop was standing with Lefebvre?
I expect my future husband to keep up with the news. Following July 2026, how many bishops served the SSPX as of October that year?
If I give you four new episcopal names to remember, which is the complete group consecrated at Écône on 1 July 2026?
answers: Schreiber, Goldade, Poinsinet de Sivry and Hanappier
Schreiber, Goldade, Fellay and Tissier de Mallerais
Hanappier, Bouchacourt, Schmidberger and Poinsinet de Sivry

questions.question: Now, sweetheart, which of the four bishops consecrated in July 2026 comes from the United States?
I adore a man who knows the roots of the liturgical revival. Who restored Benedictine life at Solesmes in 1833?
If I tell you that the international Una Voce story began with a lady's appeal in 1964, can you name her?
On our bookshop date, which English traditionalist writer should you recognise as a former president of the international Una Voce federation?
You have spotted the famous 1969 'Ottaviani Intervention' on my shelf. Which pair of cardinals presented the critical study to Paul VI?
I want you to know that traditional liturgical life extends beyond one Society. Who was the FSSP's co-founder and first Superior General?
If I tuck a little Marian book into your travelling bag, which saint wrote the Treatise on True Devotion to the Blessed Virgin?
Before we travel to Fatima together, can you tell me the precise place where Our Lady first appeared to the three shepherd children in May 1917?
I want our family to know the prayers taught before the Marian apparitions. In which year did the Angel of Peace appear to the three children?
My darling, the devotion of the Five First Saturdays has a history. In which Spanish city did Our Lady speak to Lucia on 10 December 1925?
You know the children were detained on 13 August 1917. At which place did the fourth apparition occur on 19 August instead?
If our children ask what the first part of the July 1917 Secret concerned, what will you gently and accurately tell them?
answers: The future fall of the Papal States
The discovery of a hidden chapel
An angel holding the Eucharistic host

questions.question: We would certainly say the Rosary before visiting the shrine. On which date in 1917 did the Miracle of the Sun take place?
Last Fatima question, sweetheart: how many consecutive First Saturdays and how long a meditation are requested in the devotion?
If we're to share a missal every Sunday, sweetheart, you'd better know which pope issued the 1962 edition used by the SSPX.
I whisper 'Judica me' and ask you a tiny question at the right moment: during which season does the 1962 Mass omit Psalm 42?
If the priest says 'Introibo ad altare Dei', what must my well-trained future husband know to answer as his server?
answers: Ad Deum qui laetificat juventutem meam

questions.question: Easter has arrived and I have my best chapel veil ready. Which antiphon replaces 'Asperges me' at the sprinkling?
I give you a gentle nudge after 'Orate, fratres'. What response should you know by heart at the Offertory?
answers: Suscipiat Dominus sacrificium de manibus tuis

questions.question: You may be very good at washing the teacups, but from which Vulgate Psalm does the priest say the 'Lavabo' verses?
While I follow the prayers in my lovely old missal, where should I find the 'Secret' in the order of Mass?
answers: After the Offertory and before the Preface
Between the Last Gospel and the Leonine Prayers

questions.question: You tell me you know the Roman Canon almost by heart. How does it begin, in its first two Latin words?
My ideal gentleman notices every syllable of the sacred liturgy. Where do the words 'Mysterium fidei' occur in the 1962 Canon?
answers: In the words over the chalice

questions.question: When we pray for our departed grandparents at Mass, which opening words mark the Canon's commemoration of the dead?
I'll be listening carefully towards the end of Mass. Which Gospel passage ordinarily opens the Last Gospel?
Before you promise to observe the Ember days with me, please tell me which three weekdays belong to an Ember observance.
I'd love to plan an October outing around the feast of Christ the King. When does it fall in the 1962 calendar?
answers: Sunday within the Octave of Corpus Christi

questions.question: Suppose our courtship begins in Septuagesima. What happens to the Alleluia in the traditional Roman liturgy?
answers: It is sung twice before each Gospel
It is replaced by 'Gloria in excelsis'
It is used only on Ember Saturdays

questions.question: If you hope to inherit my grandfather's old hand missal, which pope must you associate with 'Quo primum' in 1570?
I might forgive a forgotten birthday, but can you tell me who published 'Pascendi Dominici Gregis' against Modernism in 1907?
If Christ is to reign in our home, what great truth was the subject of Pius XI's encyclical 'Quas Primas'?
I have flowers ready for Our Lady's Assumption. Which apostolic constitution solemnly defined that dogma in 1950?
Before you choose a Marian name for our future daughter, which document defined the Immaculate Conception in 1854?
If we ever chant the Divine Office together, you'll need this: what did Saint Pius X's 'Divino Afflatu' principally reform?
answers: The distribution of the Psalter in the Divine Office
The calendar of the Easter Triduum

questions.question: Before I trust you to teach our children their catechism, tell me precisely what changes in transubstantiation.
answers: The visible accidents of bread and wine
The whole substance of bread and wine, while their appearances remain
The faith of the congregation without any change in the gifts

questions.question: Suppose our future teenager asks an earnest question about mortal sin. Which three conditions would you explain?
answers: Grave matter, full knowledge and deliberate consent
Public scandal, a warning and persistence

questions.question: When I ask you to pray for the holy souls in purgatory, can you explain what an indulgence actually remits?
answers: Guilt for sins not yet confessed
Temporal punishment for sins whose guilt is already forgiven

questions.question: I want our children well catechised. Which three sacraments leave an indelible spiritual character?
One final question, darling, before you ask for my hand: which session of Trent taught on the Sacrifice of the Mass in September 1562?

sharedSister.note: Lines for any Sister of Mercy without her own entry in sisters (Sisters who join the roster later). Each Sister gets her own fixed pick from these lists, so two Sisters rarely sound the same. A Sister's own entry always wins.
start: Ask whether she would ever marry you
Ask if she would consider marrying you
player: {first}, can I ask you something serious? Would you ever marry me?
{first}, I keep thinking about us. Would you consider marrying me?
I mean this, {first}. Would you ever marry someone like me?
intro: I would only marry a man who knows the faith as well as he knows me. Five questions, answered correctly one after another. A wrong answer and we start again. Ready?
Marriage is a sacrament, not a whim. I will ask you about the faith: five right in a row. Miss one and we begin again.
Then let me ask you a few things first. Five correct answers in a row and I will know you are serious. One mistake and we start over.
My grandmother would never forgive me if I married a man who did not know his catechism. Five in a row, please. Get one wrong and we go back to the beginning.
resume: Where were we? Ah, yes. Carry on.
Back again? Good. Let us continue.
Ready? Then we pick up where we stopped.
pause: Of course. Take your time, and come back to me.
We will stop here. Pray on it.
That is all right. I will be here when you are ready.
correct: That is right.
Good. Keep going.
Yes! Well done.
Correct. Next one.
You have been paying attention at Mass.
That is exactly right.
Very good. Do not stop now.
Right again. I am impressed.
wrong: No, I am afraid not. We start again.
Not quite. From the beginning.
That is not right. Let us begin again.
Oh dear. Back to the start.
No. Have another look at your catechism.
Wrong, I am sorry. Again from the top.
Close, but no. We start over.
I am afraid that is wrong. Once more, from the beginning.
pass: Five in a row. You really do know the faith. Then yes, you may ask me properly.
That is five. I did not know you had it in you. Ask me again, properly this time.
Five, all correct. I am smiling at my phone like a fool. You may propose.
noRing: Without a ring? Come back when you mean it properly.
A proposal deserves a ring. I will wait, but not forever.
I would like to say yes. I would like a ring even more.
accept: With a ring and on your word? Yes. Yes, I will marry you.
Yes. A thousand times yes. I am telling my mother straight away.
Yes. I have prayed about this, and the answer is yes.
dispute: Before I begin: you will have heard about the bishop and the review. The Sisters marry. That is one thing no chancery can take from us. Five in a row.
One thing first. The diocese is reviewing whether we should exist. I would like to answer it with a wedding. Five in a row, please.
You know about the review, I think. It makes this matter more, not less. A fellowship that marries cannot be dissolved by letter. Five in a row.
I should say it plainly: the chancery is reviewing us, and I am asking you these questions anyway, because the faith is older than the chancery. Five in a row.
Before we start: the bishop can review a fellowship. He cannot review a marriage. My mother said that first, and she is usually right. Five in a row.

thunderbirds.status: You married {name}. The Bluebirds have a new member. You won Matchfall.

victory.title: JUST MARRIED
victory.subtitle: Welcome to the Bluebirds. Welcome to the family.

underReview.success: The Foundation’s books left in a federal van the week you handed them over. The club marries you anyway. That, Celeste Van Doren says, is what family is for.
underReview.failed: The federal review came to nothing, and every Bluebird at the top table knows who asked for it. They toast you anyway. Slowly.
